Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown

instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and

correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

3. Submit only grids that your program produced.
4. After the verdict, save the program that reproduced all the pairs to the task's file, replacing any older version, then finish.

def transform(grid):
    """Overlay two equal-sized panels; mark cells where both show their common color."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    row_div = next((r for r in range(h) if len(set(grid[r])) == 1), None)
    col_div = next((c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1), None)
    if row_div is not None:
        a, b = grid[:row_div], grid[row_div + 1:]
        common = set(v for row in a for v in row) & set(v for row in b for v in row)
        # Identical panel background is the common color shared by both patterns.
        color = next(v for v in common if any(v in row for row in a) and any(v in row for row in b))
    elif col_div is not None:
        a = [row[:col_div] for row in grid]
        b = [row[col_div + 1:] for row in grid]
        common = set(v for row in a for v in row) & set(v for row in b for v in row)
        color = next(v for v in common if v != grid[0][col_div])
    else:
        raise ValueError('no solid divider')
    return [[3 if x == color and y == color else color for x, y in zip(ar, br)]
            for ar, br in zip(a, b)]", "exit_code": 0, "error": null}
